changelog: v30: Collapsible, grouped wiki sidebar. The local viewer's left nav (serve_wiki.py) is no longer a flat list of raw page paths — pages are grouped by type into collapsible sections (People, Relationships, Themes, Projects, …) with a caret, an item count, and friendly titles (frontmatter `title:`, e.g. Dad / Grandma Betty Jo / Katie under People). Top-level pages (index/log) link directly above the groups; the current page is highlighted; collapse state persists in localStorage across navigation. v29: Mention scan orders sources by salience. scan_mentions now ranks matching answers by how often the person is mentioned (descending) instead of alphabetically, so the most relevant sources survive the 14-source synthesis cap. Fixes person/Focus pages dropping important later-category material — e.g. a Focus person's death (category D) was being excluded because alphabetical order filled the cap with early A/B answers. v28: Mention-based people — the wiki grows people pages automatically. A new AI-curated roster (state/people_roster.json, built by `lifehug.py people-roster`) turns the noisy person-recommendation queue into a clean list of real, canonical people with merged aliases, role-words mapped to existing Focuses, and junk dropped. wiki_compile gains `plan_people()`: any page-eligible person (score ≥ 8 AND ≥ 2 distinct answers AND AI-confirmed real, configurable via people_page_min_score/people_page_min_answers) who isn't already a Focus gets an auto person page (origin: mention) aggregated from word-boundary mentions across all answers. Focus person pages are also enriched from cross-category mentions — so e.g. an empty Dad Focus fills in from the many places he's mentioned, while Focus behavior (question arc, planner, artifacts) is unchanged. Roster resolution is keyless on the desktop (`people-roster --emit-task`/`--from-response`) and runs after recommend-focuses in monthly_research. v27: Guard also protects legacy pages. The non-destructive compile guard now recognizes an already-synthesized page by layout (prose + `## Sources`, no `## What We Know`) when the `synthesized:` frontmatter marker is absent — so pages compiled before v26 are preserved on the first keyless compile after upgrading, instead of being downgraded to excerpts before they get re-stamped. v26: Durable, non-destructive wiki compile. The synthesis cache (state/wiki_synthesis_cache.json) is now committed to the repo, so prose synthesized on the compile machine travels to every machine and a page is only re-synthesized when its inputs change. Pages carry a `synthesized: true|false` frontmatter marker, and compile will never downgrade an already-synthesized page to a raw excerpt fallback — on a keyless machine (no cache entry, no draft, no API key) it preserves the last good prose and logs `↻ preserved <slug>` instead of clobbering it. Fixes the bug where a bare `compile` (or process_answer/daily_question auto-compile) on a machine without an API key silently replaced synthesized pages with excerpt dumps. v25: README updated to reflect v24 autonomous quality loop. Candidate lifecycle diagram now shows auto-promote/needs_review/retire flows. Big picture diagram shows quality profile feeding candidate scoring and bank retirement. Three-clocks diagram and script table updated to document auto-promotion step and age-based float. v24: Autonomous candidate promotion. weekly_maintenance now auto-promotes the highest-scoring candidates into the question bank each week with no manual action. Promotion score = candidate.priority x quality_profile.story_function_multiplier. Weekly cap is dynamic based on unanswered question count (1 when bank >120, 2 when 80-120, 3 when 40-80, 4 when <40). Per-neighborhood cap of 1 prevents any single research batch from dominating. Candidates below threshold but above 0.70 are marked needs_review. New statuses: auto_promoted, needs_review. Audit trail: promoted_by, promotion_score, promotion_reason. New CLI: lifehug.py candidates-auto-promote [--dry-run]. Weekly Telegram report includes promotion summary. v23: Fire-and-forget cron pattern. weekly_maintenance.sh and monthly_research.sh now include a telegram_notify() helper that reads telegram_chat_id from config.yaml and the bot token from TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN env or ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json (OpenClaw setups). Queue and progress output is captured and sent as a Telegram message at the end of each run — so OpenClaw crons can fire the scripts in the background and exit immediately with no timeout risk. Silent no-op when Telegram is not configured. v22: Artifact workflow. Adds `artifact.py` and `lifehug.py artifact ...` for occasion-driven letters/posts/chapters: create context packs, emit desktop/Telegram prompts, save versioned drafts, mark finals, and promote final/context artifacts into `sources/artifacts/` with provenance. Adds `/artifact` skill, post template, derived artifact source handling in wiki compile/source integrity, and updater migration for artifact sources. v21: Focus terminology migration. Replaces the legacy Focus-category vocabulary across code, CLI commands, docs, scheduler output, planner state, recommendations, and question-bank structure. Adds `focus_migration.py`, `recommend_focuses.py`, `lifehug.py recommend-focuses`, `focus-approve`, `focus-dismiss`, and `--focus-min-score`; protected implementation state is migrated forward without touching raw answers. v20.2: Monthly research loop. Adds `monthly_research.sh` and `lifehug.py monthly-research` so monthly growth is script-first: compile, report gaps, open a capped set of new research neighborhoods, refresh the self-knowledge arc when missing, recommend Focuses, report progress, and safe-autocommit. v20.1: Weekly maintenance loop. Adds `weekly_maintenance.sh` and `lifehug.py weekly-maintenance` so source lint/fix, quality profile updates, planner queue refresh, gap scan, progress report, and safe autocommit run together outside the daily question path. Source lint findings now avoid timestamp-only rewrites. v20: Source integrity layer. Raw answers and ingested stories get source metadata, manifest tracking, source lint findings, additive corrections/reflections, and all sources (including corrections/imports) compile into the private wiki. v19: Keyless desktop Focus question generation. research_expand gains `--from-response <file>`: paired with the existing `--prompt`, the agent (Claude Code) reads the emitted prompt, writes the questions JSON, and the script deposits candidates + neighborhood with no model call. The /focus skill now documents this desktop path (emit prompt → agent writes questions → deposit → promote), so adding a Focus needs no API key or gateway on the desktop; cron still uses OpenClaw/Anthropic. (serve has no model call and was already keyless.) v18: Keyless desktop wiki synthesis. `compile --emit-tasks <path>` writes per-page synthesis tasks (sources + related candidates) with no model call; the agent (Claude Code) writes each page's prose to state/synthesis/<slug>.md, and the next `compile` consumes those drafts into the cache and assembles the graph — so /compile runs on the desktop with no API key or gateway. Synthesis source order per page: cache → agent draft → OpenClaw/Anthropic (cron) → excerpt fallback. Related links are taken from an optional `Related:` line or inferred from [[wikilinks]] in the prose. v17: Wiki becomes a navigable graph. wiki_compile rewritten as plan→synthesize→cross-link→write: pages are now LLM-synthesized prose with content-derived related links (OpenClaw-first, Anthropic fallback, deterministic excerpt fallback when no LLM), plus auto-derived backlinks and shared-source 'see also' edges. Syntheses are cached in state/wiki_synthesis_cache.json so re-compiles are idempotent and cheap (--no-ai forces offline mode; new wiki_model config key). serve_wiki now resolves [[wikilinks]] to real pages (slug→page index with type-priority collision handling) instead of always bouncing to search. New `/compile` Claude Code/Desktop skill drives `lifehug.py compile` (now with --no-ai/--model passthrough). v16.1: Answer quality loop — implicit richness scoring accumulates per answer; weekly profile aggregation feeds multipliers into planner weights and AI expansion prompts; zero friction. v16: Guided Focus manager. One-shot `lifehug.py focus-new` scaffolds a new question-bank category, registers the Focus, and auto-generates+promotes ~8-12 starter questions (graceful scaffold-only fallback when no AI is available). New `/focus` Claude Code skill and OpenClaw message protocol walk through add/show/finish/tune. Adds category scaffolding (roadmap.scaffold_category) and bulk candidate promotion (candidates promote-neighborhood). Includes v15.1: OpenClaw-first AI routing in research_expand (keyless generation when OpenClaw is running; Anthropic SDK fallback). v15: Focus model + dynamic Focus-weighted allocation + self-knowledge/relational neighborhoods + wiki relationships/self surfaces + progress dashboard + three-tier scheduling.
